newsitem.title: USA: NY/NJ Port Auth to raise spending, cut jobs - paper.
newsitem.headline: NY/NJ Port Auth to raise spending, cut jobs - paper.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey plans to raise spending 19 percent to $3.1 billion but avoid increasing fares and tolls partly by cutting 500 employees, the Newark Star Ledger said on Saturday.

The paper, which cited a preliminary draft of the bi-state agency's 1997 budget that it obtained, said the plan would avoid raising fares on the PATH subway trains or increasing tolls at the Authority's bridges and tunnels.
A spokesman for the Authority on Monday said that the budget might be altered between now and the November 21 meeting by the commissioners, when they will examine the proposal.
"The board likely would vote on the budget at the regular monthly meeting of December 12," he added.

The Authority this year cut 951 jobs through offering retirement incentives and using layoffs, a 10 percent reduction in the workforce, the paper said. Two months ago, the agency put forth a new early retirement package for 1,250 employees, and about half said they would consider taking it, a decision they must make in two weeks, the Ledger said.
The paper also included the following details about the new budget proposed for 1997.

--Cutting the operating budget by $80 million to $1.43 billion. The reductions include $30 million from payroll, $34 million from service and maintenance contracts, and $34 million in administrative expenses, it said.

--Offsetting the savings would be an $11 million rise in outside contracts, and a $47 million increase in debt service for financing special private sector projects at John F Kennedy International Airport in New York City.

--Capital projects would total $1.2 billion, including $26 million to build a permanent ferry terminal at Battery Park City, $22 million for electronic toll collection at bridges and tunnels, $1.8 million on the half-mile extension of one of Newark International Airport's runways and $919,000 to modify PATH turnstiles to accept the electronic fare card used by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.

--Income is projected flat at $2.2 billion. Rents from the World Trade Center, airports, marine terminal and other facilities are seen at $802 million, with tolls and fares generating $558 million and airliner taking fees $323 million.
--The budget assumes that settlements with its labor unions will be "cost neutral" and that New York City will lose an arbitration case in which it is seeking $543 million in back rent.
